# Document Scope Clause

Qualifies initialized target documents against an approved Blue pattern and installs operation grants tied to each target’s initial identity. Registration records qualification; it neither executes a granted operation nor consumes usage.

## Configuration

`bindings.documents` is required. `bindings.pattern` and `bindings.budget` are optional. Each supplied binding must be a non-root document pointer; none has a default path.

- **`bindings.documents`** identifies the registry where candidate documents are stored, keyed by the identity of their `/contracts/initialized/document`.
- **`bindings.pattern`** supplies the approved object-valued pattern. Without this binding, `parameters.documentPattern` must supply that object. Installation freezes the pattern into the native matcher and snapshots a bound pattern. Later changes to the bound value do not replace the installed matcher, and a candidate cannot provide its own matcher.
- **`bindings.budget`** identifies shared usage state. Registration requires its `/limit` to be an integer. Installed grants require live `/used` to be strictly below live `/limit`. Registration itself does not test whether usage is exhausted, initialize these values or increment usage. Without this binding, this clause adds no usage cap. The supplied definitions do not establish usage units or accounting rules.
- **`parameters.grants`** supplies grant entries. Each entry must contain text values at `target.channel` and `target.operation`. An empty collection installs no grants.
- **`parameters.embedDocuments`** must be Boolean when supplied. Omission or `true` adds the registered-document collection to embedded processing. `false` disables that addition, for example when an already embedded producer supplies the documents’ live events. Connections can independently request embedding of their sources.

Changing an existing clause’s configuration requires a new clause key under the inherited transition validation.

## Registration and installed grants

The `register` action takes `document`, defaulting to `trigger.document`; connection `params` can override this default.

Registration proceeds only while the executing document’s `/status` equals `Active`. When `parameters.requireAttributed` is exactly `true`, it also requires:

- `processingEvent/actor` to equal `/contracts/authorizedActorChannel/actor`;
- `processingEventSource/onBehalfOf/mandate` to exist and have the same identity as the executing document’s `/contracts/initialized/document`.

Failure of either gate returns without registration. These checks concern the processing event, not the current reader’s permission.

The action rejects a missing or non-object approved pattern, a candidate that fails the frozen matcher, a missing candidate `/contracts/initialized/document`, or a bound budget whose `/limit` is not an integer. These checks precede duplicate detection. If the registry already contains the candidate’s initial identity, the action returns without replacing the stored candidate, reinstalling grants or emitting another qualification event.

For a new identity, registration stores the candidate and copies each grant into `/scope`, using a key derived from the clause key, initial identity and grant key. A grant without text `target.channel` and `target.operation` is rejected. Each copy:

- replaces `target.initialDocument` with the candidate’s initial document;
- replaces `target.documentValidation` with the approved pattern and a predicate requiring `Active`, the optional shared-budget check, and the original `target.documentValidation.function.expr` when supplied, otherwise `true`.

Other fields formerly inside `target.documentValidation` are replaced. The installed validation rechecks the pattern when the grant is used; qualification is not permanent exemption from validation.

A successful new registration emits **Document Qualified**, whose `clause` is the clause key and whose `document` is the candidate’s initial document. This records qualification and registration, not execution or completion of any granted operation.

## Connections and timing

`bindings.register` can supply named connections. This type declares no automatic registration trigger. Supported sources are `workflow`, `event`, `channel`, `embedded`, `collection`, `change`, `initialized`, `activated` and `timer`. `initialized` observes Clauses Initialized; `activated` observes Document Activated. Workflow connections require a named authenticated channel, selected by `party` when supplied or otherwise `channel`. Embedded and collection sources use `path` and request embedding unless `embed` is `false`.

Connection `when` evaluating false skips execution; a false `parameters.conditions.register` rejects it. Configured `before` steps run before the action body, so they can run even when registration subsequently returns early. `after` steps run only when the action reaches them. `once` defaults to `false`; when enabled, reaching the end of the action and `after` steps records `fired=true` and suppresses subsequent attempts. Early returns do not set that flag. It does not represent timer delivery or target-operation completion.

A timer connection requires exactly one of:

- `timestamp`: an absolute Unix-microsecond deadline from 0 through 9007199254740991; `delayMs` and `policy` are prohibited with this form;
- `afterEvent`: a source selector with positive integer `delayMs`, at most 9007199254740 milliseconds. Initialization cannot be its relative-time source. `policy` defaults to `first`; `latest` permits replacement on subsequent source events unless once-only completion already suppresses arming.

`first` arms only while `armed` is false. Arming sets that flag, and neither firing nor `cancelOn` clears it here, so cancellation does not enable another `first` arming. `cancelOn` must name a nonempty source and emits a keyed cancellation request.

Timer and cancellation requests become effective only on commit through the supported Time runtime. A request is not a firing, and `armed` does not prove a timer remains pending. Firing requires runtime admission of the pending registration and may occur late; its logical timestamp remains the requested deadline. Requests emitted after a timestamped invocation must have a deadline strictly later than that invocation’s logical time.
